question: What are the mean and the maximum request latency, and how many requests are in the data?

ports.name: mean_latency_s
ports.description: Mean latency. Round half up to 3 decimals.

ports.name: max_latency_s
ports.description: Maximum latency. Round half up to 3 decimals.

ports.name: request_count
ports.description: Number of requests.

question: What is the net revenue, the refund rate, and how many orders had a refund?
notes: amount_cents and refund_cents are in US cents. Net revenue = total amount minus total refunds. Refund rate = total refunded / total amount.

ports.name: net_revenue_usd
ports.description: Net revenue. Round half up to 2 decimals.

ports.name: refund_rate
ports.description: Refund rate. A fraction between 0 and 1, not a percentage. Round half up to 4 decimals.

ports.name: orders_with_refund
ports.description: Orders with refund_cents > 0.

question: What is the total weight shipped, which shipment is the heaviest, and how many shipments weigh more than 10 kg?
notes: unit is kg, lb or g. 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg and 1 g = 0.001 kg. Compare to 10 kg after converting.

ports.name: total_kg
ports.description: Total weight. Round half up to 2 decimals.

ports.name: heaviest_shipment
ports.description: shipment_id of the heaviest shipment.

ports.name: count_over_10kg
ports.description: Shipments strictly heavier than 10 kg.

question: By what percentage did revenue change from the first to the last month, which month had the highest revenue, and did revenue fall in any month compared with the month before?
notes: Percent change = (last - first) / first * 100. Revenue is in USD.

ports.name: change_pct
ports.description: Percent change; 12.5 means 12.5 percent. Round half up to 1 decimals.

ports.name: best_month
ports.description: Month with the highest revenue, YYYY-MM.

ports.name: any_decline
ports.description: True if some month is lower than the month before it.

question: What was the mean daily temperature, which day was the hottest, and on how many days did the temperature exceed 30 degrees Celsius?
notes: temp_f is in degrees Fahrenheit. C = (F - 32) * 5 / 9.

ports.name: mean_temp_c
ports.description: Mean temperature. Round half up to 1 decimals.

ports.name: hottest_day
ports.description: Date of the hottest day.

ports.name: days_above_30c
ports.description: Days strictly above 30 C.

question: What is the total size of all files, which file is the largest, and what share of the total does it take?
notes: size_bytes is in bytes. 1 GiB = 1073741824 bytes.

ports.name: total_gib
ports.description: Total size. Round half up to 3 decimals.

ports.name: largest_file
ports.description: Path of the largest file.

ports.name: largest_share
ports.description: Largest file size divided by total size. A fraction between 0 and 1, not a percentage. Round half up to 3 decimals.

question: What is the total time spent in sessions, the length of the longest session, and the mean session length?
notes: Timestamps are ISO 8601 in one time zone. Session length = end - start.

ports.name: total_hours
ports.description: Total session time. Round half up to 2 decimals.

ports.name: longest_session_minutes
ports.description: Longest session, rounded half up to a whole number of minutes.

ports.name: mean_session_minutes
ports.description: Mean session length. Round half up to 1 decimals.

question: What is the mean score, what share of respondents answered, and how many did not answer?
notes: score is 1 to 5. A blank cell or the text NA means the respondent did not answer; leave those out of the mean.

ports.name: mean_score
ports.description: Mean score of answered rows. Round half up to 2 decimals.

ports.name: response_rate
ports.description: Answered rows divided by all rows. A fraction between 0 and 1, not a percentage. Round half up to 3 decimals.

ports.name: n_missing
ports.description: Rows without an answer.

question: After removing export errors, how many purchases are there, what is the total spend, and which customer spent the most in total?
notes: A row that is identical to an earlier row in every column is an export error: count it once. Rows with the same customer_id but any different value are separate purchases. spend_usd is in US dollars.

ports.name: purchases
ports.description: Purchases after removing exact duplicate rows.

ports.name: total_spend_usd
ports.description: Total spend after removing duplicates. Round half up to 2 decimals.

ports.name: top_customer_id
ports.description: customer_id with the highest total spend.

question: What is the weight-adjusted mean exam score, what share of students scored at least 60, and who scored highest?
notes: exam_pct is already a percentage (0 to 100). Weighted mean = sum(exam_pct * weight) / sum(weight). The pass share counts students (rows) with exam_pct >= 60, unweighted.

ports.name: weighted_mean_pct
ports.description: Weighted mean exam score as a percentage (0 to 100). Round half up to 2 decimals.

ports.name: pass_share
ports.description: Share of students with exam_pct >= 60. A fraction between 0 and 1, not a percentage. Round half up to 2 decimals.

ports.name: top_student
ports.description: student with the highest exam_pct.
